Subject: FinPay — follow-up / latency profile and decision criteria

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation. As discussed, I wanted to capture the key constraints so we can get a recommendation from your side: 

- Primary use: real-time fraud scoring in our card transaction path (pre-authorization).
- Peak traffic: roughly 1,200 TPS for scoring requests during high volume windows; average steady-state ~350 TPS.
- Latency requirement: 95th percentile end-to-end scoring < 120ms. Per-token latency wasn't called out on our side; we have short prompts (~30–80 tokens).
- Availability: 24/7 production; we need an incident runbook and an SLA discussion.
- Data: PCI-related PII; PCI scope team is cautious — may want private deployment if we can't guarantee isolation.

Attached: finpay-latency-stats.xlsx (traffic samples + histogram).

Next steps from our side: procurement will need a clear recommended deployment model (hosted vs dedicated vs private), an estimated monthly cost range, and a short POC plan that proves latency under peak patterns. Could you put together that recommendation and a proposed POC timeline?

Thanks —

FinPay

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the traffic sample. Pushed to Marissa and Neha for sizing and infra guidance; below is a short executive recommendation and proposed next steps.

Executive recommendation (short):
- Given your sustained average (~350 TPS) and occasional peaks up to ~1.2k TPS with a strict 95p latency target (~120ms), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) is our recommended default. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput, single-tenant GPU pools, and the ability to tune batching/kv-cache aggressively for your tail-latency needs.

When Hosted could work:
- If peaks are short (< a few minutes) and you can tolerate more variability on the 95p tail, our Hosted API with burst capacity + autoscaling is lower friction and cheaper operationally. Hosted is ideal for teams that prioritize time-to-value and minimal ops.

When Private is necessary:
- If FinPay's PCI/registry requires customer-managed networking, key management (HSM), or an on-prem air-gapped deployment, Private (VPC/on-prem) is the right path. Otherwise, Dedicated covers most isolation/compliance needs via isolated pools and strict tenancy.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Marissa/Neha to review the workbook and propose a Dedicated sizing (GPU counts, expected QPS per pool) and expected 95p token latency. (ETA: 24–48 hours)
2) We propose a 2-week POC on Dedicated: a dedicated pool sized to mimic your peak (or 50% if cost-prohibitive, plus short stress tests), run a replay of your peak traffic. We'll supply an SLO runbook and measurement dashboard.
3) Procurement needs: we will provide a draft SOW and a cost estimate for both Dedicated reserved and Hosted baseline so you can compare.

Attached: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-compare.pdf (short one-pager).

If that sounds good I can schedule a 30-min kickoff with Marissa and Neha this week to align on scope.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-compare.pdf (1 page)

Hi all — dug into the spreadsheet and ran a few back-of-envelope numbers. High-level guidance below; happy to refine during the kickoff.

Sizing notes (assumptions):
- Prompt size: 30–80 tokens; model: medium-sized encoder-decoder style we discussed (quantized).
- We target 95p inference latency (model-only) < 60ms to leave headroom for network + app-side processing to meet your 120ms E2E target.

Estimated capacity per GPU (example):
- 1 x A100 (or equivalent) - optimized stack: ~250–350 short requests/sec (depends on batching, context reuse). For very low-latency (<60ms) single-request routing we expect lower per-GPU concurrency; for higher throughput with batching latency increases.

Recommended config for FinPay (to meet 95p <120ms at peaks):
- Dedicated: start with 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool, with autoscale policy to add 2 more during flagged high-volume windows. That gives a safe peak capacity ~1,000–1,400 RPS (accounting for variance).
- Tuning: aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated flows, small batching windows (10–25ms) to preserve tail latency, and per-route routing so fraud path gets pinning to low-latency nodes.

Trade-offs:
- Hosted: cheaper to start and fully managed; may struggle to guarantee 95p at 1.2k TPS consistently unless you plan to buy burst/reserved capacity on Hosted which approaches Dedicated economics.
- Private: only needed if your compliance team insists on customer-managed networking or an on-prem requirement. Otherwise Dedicated provides tenancy/isolation and KMS integration.

POC suggestion:
- 2-week Dedicated POC. Week 1: deploy Dedicated pool with 4 GPUs, run synthetic mixed traffic to verify 95p model latency <60ms. Week 2: replay FinPay traffic from your spreadsheet (we'll need the redacted replay file) and measure E2E. Deliverable: dashboard, runbook, and a short findings doc.

I'll join the kickoff and own the POC execution; Neha will help with build/deploy and monitoring hooks.

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
